title: The Herd Doesn't Take Weekends
tagline: A hundred and twenty cows, a milking parlor that runs on schedule no matter what, and one animal that's clearly not right this morning.

wake_up.text: Milking starts at 4:30, every day, weekends and holidays included. The cows don't know the difference and wouldn't care if they did.

choices.text: Check the weather report before heading to the barn
Head straight to the barn

barn_arrival.text: The barn is loud with the particular sound of a hundred and twenty cows who know exactly what time it is.

choices.text: Begin the morning milking

random_moment.text: The morning milking routine has its own small rhythm — mostly the same, a little different every day.

choices.text: The morning's milk yield comes in noticeably strong
A minor equipment hiccup slows down one milking line
The herd is unusually calm and easy this morning

sick_cow_notice.text: One of your best milkers is off her feed and standing apart from the herd — not a good sign this early in the morning.

choices.text: Take a closer look

sick_cow_decision.text: Her temperature is up and she's showing signs that could be early mastitis or something more serious — and it's a two-hour drive round trip for the vet if you call now, on a morning already full of chores.

choices.text: Call the vet immediately, whatever the morning's schedule looks like
Start treatment yourself with what you have on hand
Isolate her from the herd and monitor through the morning
Finish the rest of the herd's milking before dealing with her

cow_outcome_vet.text: The vet catches it early — a treatable infection that would have spread through the herd's udders if it waited even one more day. Expensive call, exactly the right one.

choices.text: Continue the morning's chores

cow_outcome_self.text: Your own treatment helps, and by midmorning she's improved enough that the vet visit, when it happens later, is more precautionary than urgent — a reasonable, capable call.

choices.text: Continue the morning's chores

cow_outcome_monitor.text: She holds steady through the morning under close watch, not worse but not clearly better — a reasonable wait-and-see call that costs nothing but attention.

choices.text: Continue the morning's chores

cow_outcome_delay.text: By the time the rest of the herd is milked, her condition has clearly worsened — the delay cost real time on something that needed attention right away.

choices.text: Call the vet now

midday_chores.text: Feed deliveries, fence repairs, and the equipment maintenance list that never actually gets shorter.

choices.text: Fix the back fence properly instead of a quick patch
Quick patch now, proper fix another day

afternoon_calving.text: A cow due any day now is showing early signs of labor — not urgent yet, but worth keeping an eye on through the afternoon.

choices.text: Stay close to the barn through the afternoon
Continue your normal afternoon work and check periodically

evening_milking.text: Evening milking, the second of the day's two sessions, the whole herd cycling through again exactly like clockwork.

choices.text: Do a thorough health check on every cow while milking
Keep to the standard milking routine

end_shift.text: The barn quiets down for the night. Tomorrow at 4:30, all of it starts again, exactly the same and never quite the same.

choices.text: Head in for the night

triumphant.title: The Herd Never Looked Better
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the hard one this morning. This is the kind of day that keeps a herd healthy for years.

steady_hand.title: Solid Day's Work
steady_hand.blurb: No emergencies that got away from you — just careful, attentive farming, chore after chore.

ordinary_day.title: Another Day on the Farm
ordinary_day.blurb: A full day of milking, feeding, and fixing things. Tomorrow starts at 4:30 exactly the same.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through both milkings, but your body is telling you exactly what that cost. This pace needs real rest.

written_up.title: A Hard Conversation with the Vet
written_up.blurb: Something about today's herd health call is going to need explaining. The herd is safe. The judgment call still needs a look.
